At fixed $x=(x_1+x_2)/2$ the two weighted roofs give loss $\varepsilon(1+x_1-x)$. Its minimum is at $x_1=\max(-1,2x-1)$, since $x_2=2x-x_1$ must be in $[-1,1]$. Thus the minimum is $\varepsilon|x|$. The point at height $-1$ is available for each feasible $x_1,x_2$, and vertical convexity fills the interval up to the optimized roof. This proves the entire interpolated body is the pentagon with roof $1-\varepsilon|x|$. Integrating $1+x$, $1-x$, and $|x|$ over $[-1,1]$ gives total losses $2\varepsilon,2\varepsilon,\varepsilon$ relative to $K$. On $[-1,0]$ the integrals are $1/2,3/2,1/2$, and on $[0,1]$ they are $3/2,1/2,1/2$.

For every specified pair of fibers, the lifted hull has exactly the two prescribed integer fibers, since they sit at the extreme sites of $[0,1]$. Both sites are strictly exposed, so accepted fact 2acc8bc803acf1c0 gives equality of mixed and ordinary raw depth on each. The maximum ordinary depth of a centrally symmetric body is half its volume, by symmetry at its center and the two complementary cuts through any point. Hence the original global raw maximum is $2$ and its normalized value is $\beta=3/10$. The two caps $\pm x-2z\ge0$ each have mass $2$ and cover the base-$0$ plane. The caps $\pm x+2(z-1)\ge0$ have mass $4/3$ and cover the base-$1$ plane. In particular the first two are genuinely globally critical and the other two are slack. The integer tilts exclude the opposite planes' fiber traces strictly, using $|x|\le1$ on both bodies.

In both branches, the same deformation of $B$ has area $8/3-\varepsilon$, by multiplying its width $4/3$ by its height $2-3\varepsilon/4$. Its trace in either critical cap remains empty. Each branch has total loss $3\varepsilon$. The mean critical-cap losses are $\varepsilon$ in both rows, giving first signed payments $1-3\beta=1/10$. The true Minkowski interpolation has total loss $2\varepsilon$ and critical-cap losses $\varepsilon/2$ in both rows, giving $1/2-2\beta=-1/10$. Here each signed payment is the cap loss rate minus $\beta$ times the total loss rate.

The separate path with rectangle roof $1-\varepsilon$ has exactly the mean cap and total losses. Its base-$0$ body remains centrally symmetric. Its maximum raw ordinary depth $2-\varepsilon$ exceeds the base-$1$ maximum $4/3-\varepsilon/2$ for $0<\varepsilon<1$. Exposed-fiber equality therefore gives the global normalized depth $(2-\varepsilon)/(20/3-3\varepsilon)<3/10$ on that path.

For the first branch and fixed $\eta>0$, the support at $(\eta,1)$ for sufficiently small $\varepsilon$ comes from the right end of the roof. The corresponding quotient $(h_K-h_{K_1(\varepsilon)})/\varepsilon$ is $2$. For $\eta\le0$ it comes from the left end and is $0$. After division by $\sqrt{1+\eta^2}$ to use unit normals, the pointwise limit still jumps at the upper normal. Continuous support quotients therefore fail to converge uniformly.
statement:
Let $0<\varepsilon<1$ and $K=[-1,1]^2$. For $r=1,2$ let $K_r(\varepsilon)$ have horizontal interval $[-1,1]$, lower height $-1$, and roof $1-\varepsilon(1+(-1)^{r+1}x)$. Their half-Minkowski sum has roof $1-\varepsilon|x|$ and area $4-\varepsilon$, while each branch has area $4-2\varepsilon$. The losses in the cap $x\le0$ relative to $K$ are $\varepsilon/2,3\varepsilon/2,\varepsilon/2$ for the two branches and the interpolant respectively. In $x\ge0$ the first two losses are exchanged.

At integer base $0$ put $K$, and at base $1$ put $B=[-2/3,2/3]\times[-1,1]$. Their actual lifted hull has normalized maximum depth $\beta=3/10$, and the caps $\pm x-2z\ge0$ are globally critical. The two caps $\pm x+2(z-1)\ge0$ cover the other base with strict slack. In both branches replace $B$ by $[-2/3,2/3]\times[-1+3\varepsilon/8,1-3\varepsilon/8]$. The mean of the two critical row vectors has first cap losses $(1,1)$ and first total loss $3$, giving signed payments $(1/10,1/10)$. The actual half-Minkowski path has cap losses $(1/2,1/2)$ and total loss $2$, giving signed payments $(-1/10,-1/10)$. A separate rectangle at base $0$ with roof $1-\varepsilon$ realizes the mean vector and has normalized global depth $(2-\varepsilon)/(20/3-3\varepsilon)<3/10$. The first branch's fixed-direction support quotients have a discontinuous pointwise limit at the upper facet normal, so their convergence on the unit circle is not uniform.
